name: Iberian Islamic

description.short: Eight centuries of Islamic building in Iberia and its continuation as Mudejar craft under Christian rule.
description.long:
Al-Andalus produced an architecture organized around the courtyard, water, shade, and geometric surface — a set of moves for hot-dry climates that has never been improved on. Its influence on Spanish building did not end with the Reconquest; Muslim craftsmen continued working for Christian patrons for centuries, a tradition called Mudejar.

That continuity is a transmission edge, not an imitation. The same guilds, the same masons, the same techniques — only the patron changed. It is the clearest case in the taxonomy of a craft tradition outliving the culture that produced it, and a caution against reading architectural lineage off political history.

defining_characteristics: Courtyard and water as the organizing elements of the plan
Geometric surface ornament in tile, brick, and carved plaster
Horseshoe and multifoil arches, intricate timber ceilings
Craft continuity across a political and religious rupture
